paragraphs: Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in Bangalore handle highly sensitive proprietary algorithmic trading IP, defense aerospace engineering specs, and confidential corporate research. Deploying advanced open-weight reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 via public API endpoints violates corporate data sovereignty covenants, triggers export control compliance breaches, and exposes unreleased product IP to multi-tenant cloud interception.

Our sovereign architecture deploys DeepSeek-R1 (671B MoE and distilled variants) within an air-gapped, on-premises private datacenter enclave. The infrastructure leverages multi-node FP8 execution on dedicated GPU clusters interconnected by 3.2 Tbps InfiniBand fabrics. Telemetry daemons monitor tensor parallelism ranks, inter-node all-to-all communications, and attention memory usage without touching public network interfaces.

The inference state machine enforces strict role-based access control and payload verification. Incoming reasoning prompts are validated against enterprise DLP (Data Loss Prevention) rules at the perimeter gateway. The inference orchestrator dynamically allocates reasoning tokens, monitoring token-by-token Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation while maintaining sub-15ms Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and verifying complete context privacy.

Delivering sustained throughput of 2,400 tokens per second per server node with zero external cloud egress, the solution satisfies all requirements of the DPDP Act 2023, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 Type II compliance frameworks, enabling Bangalore GCCs to run deep autonomous reasoning on sensitive IP with absolute cryptographic confidentiality.

faqs.question: What physical infrastructure is required to host DeepSeek-R1 671B in an air-gapped GCC?
faqs.answer: The full 671B MoE model requires a minimum cluster of 8x NVIDIA H100/H200 80GB SXM5 nodes with 3.2 Tbps InfiniBand interconnects for low-latency FP8 execution.

faqs.question: Does the system retain prompt history or fine-tuning weights outside the sovereign enclave?
faqs.answer: No. All KV cache pages, attention states, and logs reside exclusively in volatile GPU VRAM and encrypted local NVMe storage, wiped automatically on session termination.

faqs.question: Can GCC enterprise security teams audit the reasoning paths generated by the model?
faqs.answer: Yes. The telemetry pipeline exports cryptographically signed Chain-of-Thought execution logs directly to internal SIEM systems like Splunk or Elastic.
